e5cab69d: Who is the main hero of the series Vikings?
Ragnar Lothbrok is the farmer who becomes king, a legendary explorer who leads the first Viking raids on England.
e8e7cf51: Which English site is attacked in the first raid?
Lindisfarne is the monastery attacked in 793 AD, the historical event that marks the start of the Viking Age in English chronicles.
6bc34b56: Who is the brilliant shipbuilder of the series?
Floki is the deeply mystical master shipwright, devoted to the Norse gods and hostile to Christianity.
d5e600d8: Which of Ragnar's brothers betrays the Vikings to side with the Franks?
Rollo betrays the Vikings to marry Gisla and become Duke of Normandy, ancestor of the Normans who would invade England in 1066.
1c900650: Who is Ragnar's first wife, a formidable warrior?
Lagertha is the shieldmaiden and Ragnar's first wife, one of the strongest female characters in the series.
d1ee4a6d: What is the name of Ragnar and Lagertha's eldest son?
Björn Ironside is the son of Ragnar and Lagertha. He becomes a great king and an explorer of the Mediterranean.
7e342b40: Which English monk becomes Ragnar's close friend?
Athelstan is the Lindisfarne monk captured during the first raid, a symbol of the clash and exchange between two cultures.
65077fc5: What is the name of Ragnar's son born with brittle bones?
Ivar the Boneless is born with a bone disease. Despite his disability, he becomes one of the most formidable Viking strategists.
682f5f81: Who is the chief god of the Norse pantheon in the series?
Odin, the All-Father, is the god of wisdom, war and death. Ragnar is especially devoted to him.
7516b5d9: What is the name of the paradise of warriors who die in battle?
Valhalla is Odin's hall, where warriors slain in battle feast while awaiting Ragnarök.
e50865a1: Which English king does Ragnar mainly face in the early seasons?
Ecbert of Wessex is the most complex and intelligent king Ragnar faces, and their relationship mixes admiration and rivalry.
0a9c7347: What is the name of the Vikings' ritual method of execution?
The blood eagle is a ritual torture in which the victim's ribs are broken open to pull out the lungs. In the series, it is the fate Ragnar's sons inflict on King Aelle.
0ec0cf8e: Who kills Ragnar by throwing him into a snake pit?
King Aelle of Northumbria has Ragnar thrown into a snake pit, which drives his sons to raise the Great Heathen Army to avenge him.
71cb5995: What is the name of the great Viking army that comes to avenge Ragnar?
The Great Heathen Army invaded England in 865, as recorded in the Anglo-Saxon chronicles.
3dc664fa: Who is the Norse god of thunder?
Thor is the god of thunder and a son of Odin. His hammer Mjölnir protects gods and men, and he was the most popular god among warriors.
9bfdf9b2: What is the name of the cosmic tree that links the nine worlds?
Yggdrasil is the immense cosmic ash tree whose roots reach into the nine worlds, the axis of the Norse cosmos.
01441f81: What is the name of the rainbow bridge linking Midgard to Asgard?
Bifröst is the rainbow bridge guarded by Heimdall, linking the world of humans to the realm of the gods.
a465209c: What is the name of the Vikings' main town in the series?
Kattegat is the town where Ragnar and his people live. It is named after the strait between Denmark and Sweden.
41881d4b: Who is Halfdan, Björn's companion on his adventures?
Halfdan is the brother of King Harald Finehair. He joins several Viking expeditions and travels as far as the Mediterranean with Björn.
026c5a90: What is the name of Floki's faithful partner?
Helga follows Floki on his voyages despite the danger, and her death is one of the saddest moments of the series.
8f49f9f6: What are the female figures who choose the slain for Odin called?
The Valkyries choose the fallen warriors worthy of Valhalla. They appear in Ragnar's visions.
9f2c33a2: Which king tries to unite Norway under his crown in the series?
Harald Finehair is traditionally considered the first king of a united Norway, a 9th-century figure.
016cd649: What is the Viking runic alphabet called?
The Futhark is the Viking runic alphabet. Runes also had a spiritual dimension and were used for divination: according to myth, Odin discovered them after nine nights hanging from Yggdrasil.
67f24182: Which city becomes the capital of Rollo's duchy?
Rouen becomes the capital of Normandy, granted to Rollo by the Frankish king Charles the Simple in 911.
501a38f2: Which place does Floki believe to be the home of the gods?
Floki reaches Iceland, which he takes for the home of the gods. He tries to found a community there, which fails tragically.
a56775fd: In the series, who is the real father of Alfred, the future Alfred the Great?
In the series, Alfred is the son of Judith and the monk Athelstan, even though he is raised as Æthelwulf's son.
c182a84b: What is the role of skalds in Viking society?
Skalds are the poet-storytellers who compose verse about warriors' exploits and the deeds of the gods, passing on oral history.
46aa0c80: What did the Vikings call the North American land reached by Leif Erikson?
Vinland refers to the North American coast reached by Leif Erikson around the year 1000. The site of L'Anse aux Meadows, in Newfoundland, bears witness to it.
1d66b7e8: Björn “Ironside”: according to legend, no weapon could pierce his sides. He is a semi-legendary 9th-century figure.
00e70a38: What is the name of the sacred Swedish site of ritual sacrifices?
Uppsala is the sacred site where, according to medieval accounts, great sacrifices took place every nine years, with humans and animals hanged from trees.
25a7cd16: Which sacred animal is associated with Odin as his messenger?
The ravens Huginn (Thought) and Muninn (Memory) are Odin's messengers: they fly across the world and report everything back to him.
a5d13dfb: What is the name of the final cosmic battle of Norse mythology?
Ragnarök is the Norse end of days, the great battle in which gods and giants destroy each other.
e031e0cc: What is the name of Loki's son who is the world serpent?
Jörmungandr, the World Serpent, encircles the world biting its own tail. He and Thor kill each other at Ragnarök.
78ea4be0: What are the female beings who weave the fate of humans called?
The Norns (Urðr, Verðandi and Skuld) weave fate beneath Yggdrasil: past, present and future.
de6b535c: What is the name of Odin's eight-legged horse?
Sleipnir is Odin's eight-legged horse, born of Loki in the form of a mare, and the fastest of all horses.
b847b0c4: Who is Ragnar's second wife, the mother of Ivar?
Aslaug is the princess Ragnar meets on his travels. She becomes his second wife and the mother of Ivar.
25753eac: What was the elite guard of the Byzantine emperors, made up of Vikings, called?
The Varangian Guard was the Byzantine emperors' elite force of Scandinavian warriors, active from the late 10th century to the early 13th.
beab29a8: What is the iconic type of Viking warship?
The longship is the Viking warship: long, slender and fast, able to sail up rivers. The dragon head on its prow intimidated enemies.
9db70556: What is the name of the Norse sea goddess who captures drowned sailors?
Rán is the sea goddess who gathers drowned sailors in her net. The Vikings feared her, as she did not lead to Valhalla.
57c8ebad: Who was Rollo in historical reality?
Duke of Normandy, ancestor of William the Conqueror
Rollo (Hrólfr) received Normandy from the Frankish king Charles the Simple in 911. He was an ancestor of William the Conqueror, who invaded England in 1066.
ef75ba54: What sets Ragnar apart from other Viking chiefs in the series?
Ragnar stands out for his intellectual curiosity and openness: he takes an interest in Christianity, new lands and foreign ideas.
6e5db835: Which mysterious character resembling Odin wanders into Kattegat?
Harbard is a mysterious wanderer with supernatural powers. Clues suggest he is Odin in disguise, a classic figure of Norse mythology.
217c0279: What are the vengeful undead of Norse belief called?
The draugr are the undead of Norse mythology, vengeful spirits said to haunt the living.
394161c3: What is the historical name of the Viking raiders who settled in Russia?
The Varangians are the Vikings who settled in what is now Russia and Ukraine, opening trade routes and founding the first Kievan Rus' state around 880 AD.
4844cc29: Which female warrior builds her own army after leaving Ragnar?
Lagertha leaves Ragnar when he takes Aslaug as his second wife. She becomes an earl and commands her own army.
a3447a77: Which Frankish king offers his daughter Gisla and land to Rollo?
In the series, Charles, king of the Franks, gives his daughter Gisla and Normandy to Rollo in exchange for protection against further Viking raids.
2311dc78: What is the Viking shipbuilding technique of overlapping planks called?
Clinker building overlaps the planks so that each one laps over the next, making the hull light, flexible and watertight.
a87853d8: What is the Norse name for the human world in Viking cosmology?
Midgard is the world of humans in Norse cosmology, literally the “middle enclosure”, surrounded by the ocean.
10e445eb: Who is Freyr in Norse mythology?
The god of fertility and harvests
Freyr is the god of fertility, harvests, rain and sunshine. With his sister Freyja, he belongs to the Vanir.
59fc65b7: According to Norse mythology, what is unique about Freyr's sword?
It can cut through any metal
It fights on its own, with no one holding it
Freyr's sword fights by itself. He gives it to his servant Skírnir to win the giantess Gerðr, which leaves him unarmed at Ragnarök.
587c4858: What is the name of the giant wolf who devours Odin at Ragnarök?
Fenrir is the giant wolf, son of Loki, chained by the gods because he was too powerful. He breaks free at Ragnarök and devours Odin, before being killed by Víðarr, Odin's son.
b239b1fb: Who is Tyr in Norse mythology?
The god of justice and combat
Tyr is the god of law, justice and combat. He loses his hand by placing it in Fenrir's jaws so the gods can chain the wolf.
f8c1176f: What is the most spectacular Viking funeral custom?
Ship cremation was reserved for high-ranking warriors: the ship burned, symbolizing the journey to the afterlife.
2fc3220a: Who is Skaði in Norse mythology?
Keeper of the apples of immortality
Skaði is the goddess of mountains, hunting and skiing, a giantess who joins the Æsir after demanding a husband from among them.
651e3b04: Which precious metal was most widely used in Viking trade?
Silver was the Vikings' standard of value: hacksilver, weighed pieces of silver, served as currency along all the trade routes.
9baa3584: What is the name of the Norse goddess of love and magic?
Freyja is the goddess of love, fertility, war and seiðr magic. She receives half of the slain warriors in her field, Fólkvangr.
7f80fa48: Which animal is the attribute of the goddess Freyja?
Freyja rides a chariot drawn by two cats and owns a cloak of falcon feathers.
6f6dd1bd: What is the trade route between Scandinavia and Byzantium called?
The route “from the Varangians to the Greeks” ran from the Baltic to the Black Sea, linking Scandinavia to Constantinople via the Russian rivers.
9a29165b: Who is Iðunn in Norse mythology?
The keeper of the apples of immortality
Iðunn keeps the apples that keep the gods forever young. When the giant Þjazi abducts her, the Æsir begin to age.
57003d8f: What is the name of the serpent that gnaws at the roots of Yggdrasil?
Níðhöggr gnaws endlessly at one of Yggdrasil's roots, deep in the underworld.
85ddc9f0: What were the main Viking exports to the East (Byzantium)?
The two great Viking exports to the East were slaves (thralls) and precious furs, traded for silk, spices and silver.
f32595d7: Who is Baldr in Norse mythology?
The god of light, the most beloved of the Æsir
Baldr, son of Odin and Frigg, is the god of light and purity. His death, caused by Loki with a sprig of mistletoe, is one of the most famous Norse myths.
